findings.title: Increment the retry counter atomically
findings.body: Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before processing the batch. If cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they write the same value, so two failed attempts are recorded as one and the reminder remains eligible for further attempts instead of reaching the deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation in both failure paths.

findings.title: Do not let failure bookkeeping abort the entire batch
findings.body: The catch block now awaits a Prisma update without handling errors from that update. If a reminder is deleted while the batch is processing (for example, by an overlapping cleanup invocation), the update throws a record-not-found error out of the catch block. This aborts the cron request and skips every remaining reminder in the batch; previously the scheduling error was logged and processing continued. Handle bookkeeping failures separately, including reminders that no longer exist, so one failed reminder cannot stop the batch.
